title: Predictive Warmth Grid & Tenant Quorum — PRD proposal
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes the Predictive Warmth Grid (PWG) + Tenant Quorum system: a hybrid autoscale and isolation control that proactively allocates short-lived warm GPU slots based on tenant demand forecasting and a quorum-based admission mechanism that reduces noisy-neighbor risk during demand spikes. Target use: Dedicated customers who need predictable latency SLOs while still allowing controlled bursts and maintaining stronger tenant isolation guarantees.

Problem statement and context:
- Current dedicated pool behavior relies on reactive warm pools and simple burst credits. During sudden correlated tenant spikes we see higher tail latency and tenant interference.
- Customers ask for: predictable latency in 99th percentile, the ability to absorb microbursts without manual reserve purchases, and clear deterministic behavior when oversubscription occurs.
- Many existing PRDs focus on either autoscaling velocity or strict isolation; PWG aims to combine short-term predictive prewarm with a policy-driven admission/quorum to balance cost and isolation.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce 99th percentile latency regressions for dedicated tenants during bursts by >= 30% (measured on internal benchmark workload set).
- Allow average unit cost to increase <= 8% compared to baseline reactive warm pool strategy while improving latency stability.
- Provide deterministic admission behavior: when pool is constrained, tenants see an explicit "quorum-reject" or soft-degrade path (fallback model variant) rather than silent latency spikes.
- Ops controls: runbook for escalation, tooling to adjust PQ thresholds and forecast horizon without code rollout.

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-term reserved capacity model. PWG is not a billing model change, it's runtime capacity orchestration.
- Solving every multi-tenancy interference vector (we target compute contention and queueing, not noisy storage or network).

User stories (examples):
- As an ML infra engineer I want the autoscaler to prewarm slots for a predicted peak 60s ahead so my customer-facing latency SLOs hold through flash sales.
- As a platform PM I want to define tenant-quorum policies per-customer tier so high-tier customers have priority admission during contention.
- As a solutions engineer I want to simulate a tenant surge in staging and see deterministic fallback behavior so I can advise customers.

Design overview (high level):
1) Demand signal and forecast:
   - Ingress telemetry feeds: request rate, tokens/sec, sequence length histogram per tenant, model family and route.
   - Lightweight rolling predictor (ensemble: EWMA + short LSTM/transformer-lite) runs per-tenant and per-model-family with horizon configurable (default 60s).
2) Warmth Grid allocation:
   - Warm slots = ephemeral GPU reservations sized to a tenant's recent burst footprint (KV cache + batch concurrency).
   - Grid is a soft matrix indexed by (region, gpu-type, model-family, qos-lane). Each cell holds warm slots and aging info.
   - Predictor marks cells for prewarm; orchestrator schedules warm startup with exponential backoff and cap per-tenant to limit cost.
3) Tenant Quorum Admission:
   - When a new request arrives and active capacity is near saturation, admission controller consults tenant quorum policy: a quorum score computed from priority, recent SLA performance, and remaining warm credits.
   - Admission outcomes: allow (serve on warm slot), queue (short hold for up to Q ms), soft-fallback (serve on cheaper model-variant with lower resource profile), or reject with explicit error.
4) Fairness and decay:
   - Warm slots are decayed on inactivity with tenant-specific cooldowns to prevent churn.
   - Quorum prioritization decays to avoid starvation; a sliding window ensures tenants with sustained usage make progress.

Configuration surface (operator-facing):
- Forecast horizon (default 60s, tunable 15-300s)
- Per-tenant max warm fraction (percentage of pool)
- Quorum tiers: premium / standard / best-effort with weights and reserve buckets
- Fallback model mappings and prioritized route list
- Cost cap (auto-disable prewarm if estimated cost delta exceeds threshold)

API/telemetry contract (outline):
- New telemetry fields: forecasted_rps, forecast_uncertainty, warm_slots_assigned, quorum_score, admission_decision.
- Hooks in Console: per-route forecast heatmap, per-tenant warm-slot occupancy, and "quorum events" timeline.
- Exposed API for tenants: prewarm advisory endpoint (read-only) returning recommended warm_window and estimated prewarm cost.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE and CS):
- Alert: sustained quorum_reject_rate > 2% for > 5m -> page oncall SRE + notify customer success for affected tenants.
- Mitigation: temporarily raise premium weights or increase forecast horizon in region cell to allow more prewarm.
- Cost surge: if prewarm_cost_estimate delta >= 15% for 24h, auto-disable predictive prewarm and revert to reactive warm pool.

Safety and isolation controls:
- Strong isolation guardrail: tenant_max_warm_fraction prevents single tenant from occupying > X% of a grid cell.
- Quorum audit log: every admission decision surfaces the top-3 contributing factors (priority, forecast, occupancy) for debugging.
- Hard fallback policy: if prewarm causes cross-tenant QoS regressions, circuit breaker turns off PWG in that cell for N minutes.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal only): run PWG in simulation mode (no prewarm) using two-week historical traffic to validate forecasts. (2 weeks)
- Beta (select customers): enable predictive prewarm in a single region for 3 low-risk customers; monitor cost and 99th latency. (4 weeks)
- Canary: limited roll to customers with dedicated pools and opt-in toggle in Console. Add automatic disable on cost/latency regressions. (2 weeks)
- GA: enable API and console controls, documentation and runbook, opt-out remains available. (after monitoring milestones met)

Metrics and analysis plan:
- Primary metrics: tenant_99p_latency, quorum_reject_rate, warm_slot_utilization, prewarm_cost_delta_vs_baseline, tail_latency_p95-p999 spread.
- A/B experiment outline: 50/50 split on reserved pool instances for eligible tenants, run for 4 weeks on production traffic slices.

Open questions / design tradeoffs to resolve:
- Predictor model choice: lightweight LSTM vs purely statistical model to reduce inference cost of predictor itself.
- Warm slot sizing granularity: fixed slot sizes vs dynamic allocation per model; trade cost vs packing efficiency.
- How to bill for prewarm capacity? (We recommend keeping billing unchanged initially and surface "estimated prewarm cost" to customers.)

Risks and mitigations:
- Cost overshoot: mitigation via cost cap and auto-revert.
- Forecast misses causing prewarm waste: conservative forecast thresholds, ensemble uncertainty gating.
- Complexity of admission logic leading to obscure failures: require clear audit logs and visible "quorum explanation" in first rollout.

Notes to self / next steps (action items):
- Spike: implement lightweight predictor prototype and run against last quarter traffic (owner: Marcus).
- Run simulation harness to estimate warm slot cost tradeoffs (owner: Ben).
- Draft Console surfaces for forecast heatmap and admission events (owner: Sofia).
- Create staging chaos test for correlated tenant spikes (owner: Priya).

short_description: PRD proposal for a hybrid predictive prewarm + tenant-quorum admission system to improve latency stability for dedicated pools.
